## Multidisciplinary care for people living with chronic pain

At the Pain Collective, we provide multidisciplinary pain management services through a network of
clinics across South Africa.

Our interdisciplinary team of doctors and therapists utilises therapy, medication, patient-centred
modalities, and interventional procedures as part of pain management.

Our approach emphasises active, patient -centred care and interventional strategies where
appropriate.

As part of our commitment to transparency and ongoing quality improvement, we routinely collect
anonymous patient experience feedback and publish summary results from our monthly internal service
evaluation surveys.

**97%*** of patients who completed our anonymous monthly patient experience surveys reported being
satisfied with their overall experience at our clinics.

**92%*** of patients who completed our anonymous patient experience surveys after a theatre
procedure reported that the procedure met their expectations.

**91%*** of patients who completed our anonymous patient experience surveys reported that they felt
the service represented good value for money.

**85%*** of patients reported that their doctor listened to them attentively, and 81% reported that
their doctor explained information in a way they could understand, based on responses to our
anonymous patient experience surveys.

**88%*** of patients who attended therapy services reported that the care they received from the
therapist was excellent, based on responses to our anonymous patient experience surveys.

These figures are based on routine, anonymous monthly patient experience surveys conducted for
internal service evaluation and quality improvement. Survey responses reflect patient-reported
experiences of care, communication, and service delivery. These data are not intended to represent
clinical outcomes, treatment efficacy, or guarantees of results.

## ABOUT US

The Pain Collective is a group of doctors and therapists who share a passion for conservative and
holistic pain management. We treat a range of conditions, including back, neck, knee, and hip pain,
as well as chronic headaches and many other similar conditions. Our aim is to diagnose and treat
pain – without surgery – through the use of an interdisciplinary team and maintenance programmes.

## NURTURING

Persistent pain is a complex condition the that needs multimodal treatment from an interdisciplinary
team. Lifestyle adaptations are the most important tool in managing long-term pain. Dietary changes,
combined with movement, physical therapy, mental health care, pain neuroscience education, and
individualised pain procedures, are key to the management of persons people living with chronic
pain. 
[PAIN PROCEDURES][139][MOVEMENT PROGRAMMES][140]

## Paediatric Pain Management

20 – 35% of Children children and Adolescents adolescents worldwide struggle with chronic pain.

Dr Rudolph Hiemstra, a paediatrician, is joining our multidisciplinary team to provide a chronic
pain management service to children and adolescents. 

[ READ MORE ][141]

## NATURE

Did you know that your genetics can make you more prone to certain types of diseases? You may have a
genetic predisposition to develop certain conditions that can cause chronic pain. Fortunately, the
things you do, the environment you are exposed to, what you eat, and how much you sleep and so on
can influence how your genes work. Making dietary changes, participating in regular physical
activity, adaptation of the activities of daily living you engage in adapting your daily activities,
fixing improving your sleep patterns, and understanding your body can make a massive difference to
your overall health and reduce your pain.

## TrueRelief is only available through healthcare professionals.

TrueRelief is FDA-cleared for relief of chronic intractable pain, and as an adjunctive treatment in
the management of post-surgical and post-traumatic acute pain. It is intended for use under the
supervision of a Healthcare Professional. TrueRelief should not be used on patients who are pregnant
or have a cardiac demand pacemaker. For a complete listing of the Indication for Use and all
contraindications, warnings, precautionsand adverse reactions please [click here][12].

## Federal grant awarded from the Health & Human Services Department

**The TrueRelief technology was awarded a $244,000 federal grant from the Health & Human Services
Department, in conjunction with the Treasury Department and the National Institutes of Health.**
* This Therapeutic Discovery Project Program was initiated by the government to improve healthcare
  by supporting biotech firms with the largest potential.
* The selection criteria was centered on identifying new technologies that offered significant
  likelihood to produce new therapies, address unmet medical needs, and reduce the long-term growth
  of healthcare costs.

## About Us

#### Management

#### **John Crosson** | President

As the angel investor behind the technology that has become TrueRelief and the chief architect of
product development, John took a single patent for a precursor version and evolved the technology to
where it is today, amassing 25 additional patents in the process (17 as the named inventor), with
more than two dozen pending applications. John has overseen all research of TrueRelief that has
ultimately been published. He has also played a critical role in establishing clinical applications
including the launch of TrueRelief’s equine use device. Outside of TrueRelief, John spent 10 years
on the board of the Crohn’s & Colitis Foundation (including three years as its Chair), during which
time he oversaw over $350 million in spending on medical research. John has over 30 years of
experience as a marketer building some of the most recognized and valuable brands in the world
including BMW, Nestle, Hilton, Gallo, and Harry Potter (for Warner Bros.), and as a CEO led a
company generating over $200 million in annual revenue.

#### Advisors

#### **Peter Armstrong ** | MD

Peter Armstrong has enjoyed a 40+ year career as both a respected pediatric orthopedic surgeon and a
business leader. Currently Chairman of the Board Emeritus of the Foundation for Advancing Pediatric
Orthopedics, Dr. Armstrong previously served for 11 years as Chief Medical Officer of
OrthoPediatrics and prior to that as Chief Medical Officer of Shriners Hospitals for Children. He
also spent nine years as Professor of Orthopedic Surgery at the University of Utah. Dr. Armstrong is
a member of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America Hall of Fame.

#### **Andrew Ekdahl**

Andrew Ekdahl has served in a variety of executive leadership roles throughout the Johnson & Johnson
Medical Devices business including Worldwide President at DePuy Synthes and President of Ethicon
Surgical Care. He is a culturally adaptable leader with a deep understanding of diverse healthcare
markets particularly in the United States, Canada, Japan and Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Mr.
Ekdahl is an expert in medical device marketing and commercialization and his 30+ years of
leadership experience include deep involvement in developing and commercializing products for
orthopedic surgeries and joint reconstruction in particular.

#### **David Hatch Jr** | DPM

David Hatch is a practicing podiatrist with a particular emphasis on the critical aspects in the
prevention and treatment of the diabetic foot including advanced wound care, re-vascularization, and
surgical foot reconstruction. In addition to his clinical practice, Dr. Hatch is a well published
researcher of foot and ankle disease and a lecturer and adjunct professor at Midwestern University.
Much of Dr. Hatch’s published research is focused on diabetic foot wounds and negative pressure
wound therapy. He has also dedicated hundreds of service hours to help others less fortunate
including at shelters where he helps address foot and ankle pathology for the needy.

#### **Mark Klaassen** | MD

Mark Klaassen is an orthopedic surgeon specializing in knee, hip and shoulder total joint
replacement, and arthroscopic surgery. Dr. Klaassen is a highly sought orthopedic surgeon, inventor
and educator who currently serves as Professor of Practice in the College of Sciences at the
University of Notre Dame. Dr. Klaassen is a fellow of the American College of Surgeons (FACS) and
the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (FAAOS). He is also an active member of numerous
medical organizations, including the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons (AAHKS), American
Medical Association (AMA), Mennonite Medical Association (MMA), American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle
Society (AOFAS), American Fracture Association (AFA), and the Indiana Orthopaedic Society.

#### **Todd Pope**

Todd Pope has nearly 30 years of healthcare experience in medical devices, pharmaceutical, and
executive management. He is currently the Executive Chairman of Innovators. Prior to this, he was
the President and CEO of TransEnterix, the Global President of Johnson & Johnson Cordis, CEO of
Liquidia Technologies and President of American Tool Company. He spent 14 years in various
management roles with increasing levels of responsibility at both Johnson & Johnson and Boston
Scientific. He was named in Time Magazine’s 50 Most Influential People in Healthcare.

#### **Kara Rood** | MD

Kara Rood is a maternal fetal medicine physician and a Clinical Associate Professor of Obstetrics
and Gynecology at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. She is also the Director of the
Substance, Abuse, Treatment, Education and Prevention Program (STEPP). Dr. Rood is actively involved
in research and is well published in peer reviewed journals and textbooks. Her research focus
includes hypertensive diseases of pregnancy, substance use and misuse during pregnancy, and
postpartum hemorrhage. She was the principal investigator of TrueRelief’s sham-controlled clinical
trial published by JAMA on their Network Open which found patients treated with TrueRelief following
cesarean section surgery consumed 47% less opioids than a like group of patients who received sham
treatments.

## TrueRelief is only available through healthcare professionals.

TrueRelief is FDA-cleared for relief of chronic intractable pain, and as an adjunctive treatment in
the management of post-surgical and post-traumatic acute pain. It is intended for use under the
supervision of a Healthcare Professional. TrueRelief should not be used on patients who are pregnant
or have a cardiac demand pacemaker. For a complete listing of the Indication for Use and all
contraindications, warnings, precautionsand adverse reactions please [click here][12].

## About Us

#### Management

#### **John Crosson** | President

As the angel investor behind the technology that has become TrueRelief and the chief architect of
product development, John took a single patent for a precursor version and evolved the technology to
where it is today, amassing 25 additional patents in the process (17 as the named inventor), with
more than two dozen pending applications. John has overseen all research of TrueRelief that has
ultimately been published. He has also played a critical role in establishing clinical applications
including the launch of TrueRelief’s equine use device. Outside of TrueRelief, John spent 10 years
on the board of the Crohn’s & Colitis Foundation (including three years as its Chair), during which
time he oversaw over $350 million in spending on medical research. John has over 30 years of
experience as a marketer building some of the most recognized and valuable brands in the world
including BMW, Nestle, Hilton, Gallo, and Harry Potter (for Warner Bros.), and as a CEO led a
company generating over $200 million in annual revenue.

#### **Peter Armstrong ** | MD

business leader. Currently Chairman of the Board Emeritus of the Foundation for Advancing Pediatric
Orthopedics, Dr. Armstrong previously served for 11 years as Chief Medical Officer of
OrthoPediatrics and prior to that as Chief Medical Officer of Shriners Hospitals for Children. He
also spent nine years as Professor of Orthopedic Surgery at the University of Utah. Dr. Armstrong is
a member of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America Hall of Fame.

#### **Andrew Ekdahl**

Andrew Ekdahl has served in a variety of executive leadership roles throughout the Johnson & Johnson
Medical Devices business including Worldwide President at DePuy Synthes and President of Ethicon
Surgical Care. He is a culturally adaptable leader with a deep understanding of diverse healthcare
markets particularly in the United States, Canada, Japan and Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Mr.
Ekdahl is an expert in medical device marketing and commercialization and his 30+ years of
leadership experience include deep involvement in developing and commercializing products for
orthopedic surgeries and joint reconstruction in particular.

#### **David Hatch Jr** | DPM

prevention and treatment of the diabetic foot including advanced wound care, re-vascularization, and
surgical foot reconstruction. In addition to his clinical practice, Dr. Hatch is a well published

wound therapy. He has also dedicated hundreds of service hours to help others less fortunate
including at shelters where he helps address foot and ankle pathology for the needy.

Mark Klaassen is an orthopedic surgeon specializing in knee, hip and shoulder total joint
replacement, and arthroscopic surgery. Dr. Klaassen is a highly sought orthopedic surgeon, inventor
and educator who currently serves as Professor of Practice in the College of Sciences at the
University of Notre Dame. Dr. Klaassen is a fellow of the American College of Surgeons (FACS) and
the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (FAAOS). He is also an active member of numerous
medical organizations, including the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons (AAHKS), American
Medical Association (AMA), Mennonite Medical Association (MMA), American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle
Society (AOFAS), American Fracture Association (AFA), and the Indiana Orthopaedic Society.

executive management. He is currently the Executive Chairman of Innovators. Prior to this, he was
the President and CEO of TransEnterix, the Global President of Johnson & Johnson Cordis, CEO of
Liquidia Technologies and President of American Tool Company. He spent 14 years in various
management roles with increasing levels of responsibility at both Johnson & Johnson and Boston
Scientific. He was named in Time Magazine’s 50 Most Influential People in Healthcare.

and Gynecology at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center. She is also the Director of the

in research and is well published in peer reviewed journals and textbooks. Her research focus
includes hypertensive diseases of pregnancy, substance use and misuse during pregnancy, and
postpartum hemorrhage. She was the principal investigator of TrueRelief’s sham-controlled clinical
trial published by JAMA on their Network Open which found patients treated with TrueRelief following

Non-Narcotic Solutions to Reduce Healthcare Costs & Enhance Recovery

# Revolutionizing Pain Management Techniques

Our commitment to reducing over-utilization of narcotics and opiates is matched only by our
dedication to providing effective modalities that support recovery after injury.

As [leaders in the industry][22], Ultra Pain Products strives to stay at the forefront of pain
management solutions and offer the latest advancements in pain relief. With a focus on practicality
and efficacy, our goal is clear: to reduce the economic burden on the healthcare system and prevent
lost working days due to injury or surgery.

Join us in embracing a healthier, more efficient approach to pain management as we introduce you to
cutting-edge [pain management devices][23]. Your patients will say goodbye to a reliance on
narcotics and welcome a future of increased functional abilities and improved quality of life.



(833) ANTI-PAIN

## A Multi-Faceted Approach to Pain Relief

Our mission goes beyond delivering pain management devices. We aim to:



### Reduce The Economic Burden On The Healthcare System

By providing safe and alternative home-based treatment modalities, we help to continue the healing
process from home – reducing the costs associated with prolonged recovery and related
complications. 



### REDUCE The USE Of Narcotic/Opioids

Our products provide a non-narcotic adjunctive therapy option to help manage pain. We believe in
promoting safer pain management practices.



### Minimize Lost Working Days For Injured Workers

For individuals affected by work-related or auto-related injuries, our solutions aid in faster
recovery and a swift return to work.

## Non-Surgical, Pain-Free Products

## Preferred PainShield Provider

Ultra Pain Products is the exclusive distributor of the [PainShield][24]® in the USA. Our focus on
work-related and auto-related injuries makes us the preferred provider for the injury community. By
offering opioid-free non-invasive pain management alternatives, we ensure patients receive the best
care possible and are on the right road to recovery.

Providing convenience and comfort, our devices are designed for effective pain management in the
comfort of your patient’s home.

alternatives.

## Shaping the Future of Health

Excellence in care, recognized worldwide. See the latest news, awards, and innovations from UTMB.

[Young patient wearing a hospital wristband sits on a bed next to a healthcare professional in
scrubs with an ID badge in a clinical room. Medical equipment and a bed are visible in the
background.]

### [From basketball court to crisis and back: UTMB Health guides a young athlete’s healing
### journey][105]

July 22, 2026, 8:53 a.m. by Margaret Battistelli Gardner and Tristen Kersh

When an ordinary basketball play left 9-year-old Jonah with a hidden brain bleed, UTMB Health
pediatric experts guided him from a frightening diagnosis to a full return to the sport he loves.

[A teenage patient smiles from her hospital bed as a therapy dog wearing a blue service vest rests
beside her. The dog provides comfort and emotional support during her hospital stay, helping create
a calmer, more reassuring environment.]

### [Therapy dogs lend a healing paw in teen's recovery at UTMB Health][106]

July 21, 2026, 8:43 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Following two major spinal fusion revision surgeries, 16-year-old Lilly Tucker spent six weeks at
UTMB Health recovering from temporary partial paralysis. During her rehabilitation, visits from dogs
in the pet therapy program provided comfort, eased anxiety, and motivated her to walk farther and
faster during physical therapy.

[A man wearing a white UTMB Health lab coat stands with his arms crossed in a clinical procedure
room. Medical imaging equipment, a patient monitor, and shelves stocked with clinical supplies
surround him, highlighting the healthcare setting.]

### [Shifts in pain management focus on safer, nonopioid treatments][107]

July 20, 2026, 2:35 p.m. by Katherine Adams

Patients seeking pain treatment are increasingly asking about alternatives to opioids. Physicians at
UTMB Health emphasize personalized care that targets the source of pain through procedures, physical
therapy, lifestyle changes, and psychological support.

[Dr. Israa Ali, wearing a brown outfit, smiles while speaking with a female patient in a blue shirt
during a weight management consultation in her office.]

### [Weight loss is one battle. Keeping it off is another.][108]

July 17, 2026, 8:33 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Weight loss and weight maintenance are two different biological processes, according to UTMB
endocrinologist Israa Ali, MD. While losing weight requires creating a calorie deficit, maintaining
that loss requires overcoming the body’s natural responses, including a slower metabolism and
increased hunger signals designed to restore lost weight.

[A woman stands smiling in a white UTMB Health lab coat while holding a stethoscope with her arms
crossed.]

### [Nishi named chief of pulmonary, critical care, and sleep medicine at UTMB][109]

July 15, 2026, 8:00 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Shawn Nishi, MD, has been appointed chief of the UTMB Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care, and
Sleep Medicine. A UTMB alumna and longtime faculty member, she aims to expand research, education,
innovation, and access to specialized pulmonary care.

## Shaping the Future of Health

Excellence in care, recognized worldwide. See the latest news, awards, and innovations from UTMB.

[Young patient wearing a hospital wristband sits on a bed next to a healthcare professional in
scrubs with an ID badge in a clinical room. Medical equipment and a bed are visible in the
background.]

### [From basketball court to crisis and back: UTMB Health guides a young athlete’s healing
### journey][105]

July 22, 2026, 8:53 a.m. by Margaret Battistelli Gardner and Tristen Kersh

When an ordinary basketball play left 9-year-old Jonah with a hidden brain bleed, UTMB Health
pediatric experts guided him from a frightening diagnosis to a full return to the sport he loves.

[A teenage patient smiles from her hospital bed as a therapy dog wearing a blue service vest rests
beside her. The dog provides comfort and emotional support during her hospital stay, helping create
a calmer, more reassuring environment.]

### [Therapy dogs lend a healing paw in teen's recovery at UTMB Health][106]

July 21, 2026, 8:43 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Following two major spinal fusion revision surgeries, 16-year-old Lilly Tucker spent six weeks at
UTMB Health recovering from temporary partial paralysis. During her rehabilitation, visits from dogs
in the pet therapy program provided comfort, eased anxiety, and motivated her to walk farther and
faster during physical therapy.

[A man wearing a white UTMB Health lab coat stands with his arms crossed in a clinical procedure
room. Medical imaging equipment, a patient monitor, and shelves stocked with clinical supplies
surround him, highlighting the healthcare setting.]

### [Shifts in pain management focus on safer, nonopioid treatments][107]

July 20, 2026, 2:35 p.m. by Katherine Adams

Patients seeking pain treatment are increasingly asking about alternatives to opioids. Physicians at
UTMB Health emphasize personalized care that targets the source of pain through procedures, physical
therapy, lifestyle changes, and psychological support.

[Dr. Israa Ali, wearing a brown outfit, smiles while speaking with a female patient in a blue shirt
during a weight management consultation in her office.]

### [Weight loss is one battle. Keeping it off is another.][108]

July 17, 2026, 8:33 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Weight loss and weight maintenance are two different biological processes, according to UTMB
endocrinologist Israa Ali, MD. While losing weight requires creating a calorie deficit, maintaining
that loss requires overcoming the body’s natural responses, including a slower metabolism and
increased hunger signals designed to restore lost weight.

[A woman stands smiling in a white UTMB Health lab coat while holding a stethoscope with her arms
crossed.]

### [Nishi named chief of pulmonary, critical care, and sleep medicine at UTMB][109]

July 15, 2026, 8:00 a.m. by Katherine Adams

Shawn Nishi, MD, has been appointed chief of the UTMB Division of Pulmonary, Critical Care, and
Sleep Medicine. A UTMB alumna and longtime faculty member, she aims to expand research, education,
innovation, and access to specialized pulmonary care.

  objective, accurate, and balanced reporting
* 02
  Maintaining **editorial independence ** and transparency into how we protect the integrity of our
